intro_html: The salmon and the ikura go all through the rice instead of hiding in the middle: salted salmon grilled until just flaking and still juicy, folded into hot rice with shiso, shio kombu and sesame, then the cold ikura folded in once the rice is warm enough to hold — every bite pink, green and popping. Shaping basics are on the onigiri page.

notes.html: Folded through the rice, the salmon and ikura are in every bite — pink and green all the way through, with no dry corner of plain rice.
notes.title_html: Why mixed through, not a filling

notes.html:
• Hot rice will cook the eggs soft and cloudy.
  • Cool the mixed rice until you can hold it, then fold the cold ikura in gently.

• Traditional salted salmon is cooked well done and dry, so it keeps in a lunch box.
  • For eating the same day, take it off as soon as it flakes — the flakes stay juicy in the rice.

• Salmon flakes from a Japanese grocery (shake flakes in a jar) work in place of grilling your own.
  • Ikura is sold in small trays, often frozen; thaw it in the fridge.

• Shio kombu and the salt on your hands both salt the rice — taste a bit of the mixed rice before shaping and go lighter on your hands if it's already well seasoned.
  • Table salt: half the amount.

• The mixed rice (salmon, shiso, myoga, shio kombu, sesame), its amounts and the shaping are Just One Cookbook's salmon and shio kombu onigiri.
  • The sake and salt on the fish and the fish grill are her shiozake, but shortened: she cures it 2 days and cooks it well done; here it's salted 20–30 minutes and taken off while still moist.
  • Folding the ikura through the rice, the chopped crisp skin and the nori strip are this site's additions.

steps.body_html:
• Wash the rice, soak it 20–30 minutes in the water, then cook it (rice cooker or pot) — the method is on the onigiri page.
  • Plain rice — no vinegar, no sugar. You need it hot for mixing.
steps.title: Cook the rice

steps.body_html:
• Sprinkle the sake over the salmon, turn it to coat and leave it 10 minutes. Pat dry with a paper towel.
  • Sprinkle the salt over the skin and both sides.
  • On a paper towel, skin side up, in the fridge for 20–30 minutes. Pat it dry again.

how.caption: Sake over, 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Salt the skin and both sides.

steps.title: Salt the salmon

uses_rows.amount_html: 150 g (1 fillet)

steps.body_html:
• Heat a fish grill (or a grill pan or frying pan) over medium heat.
  • Skin side down first, about 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp and golden.
  • Turn and cook about 4 minutes more, until the flesh is just opaque and flakes apart but still moist in the middle. Don’t take it to dry.

how.caption: Skin side down first, until the skin is crisp.
Turn it; take it off while it's still moist.

steps.title: Grill — stop while it's juicy

steps.body_html:
• Let it cool a minute, then peel off the skin.
  • Flake the flesh with chopsticks or a fork into big, juicy flakes, picking out any bones.
  • Chop the crisp skin into small bits — it goes into the rice for crunch.

how.caption: Peel off the skin, then flake the flesh into big, juicy flakes.
Chop the crisp skin into small bits.

steps.title: Flake it, chop the skin

steps.body_html:
• Cut the stems off the shiso, stack and roll the leaves from the stem end, slice into thin strips and loosen them.
  • Halve the myoga lengthwise and slice thinly (skip it if you can't find it).

how.caption: Stack the shiso, roll from the stem end, slice into thin strips.
Halve the myoga lengthwise, slice it thinly.

steps.title: Shiso and myoga

steps.body_html:
• Tip the hot rice into a large bowl or tray so there's room to mix.
  • Scatter over it:
    • shiso
    • myoga
    • shio kombu (salted kelp strips) 1½ tbsp
    • toasted white sesame seeds 2 tsp
    • the salmon flakes and chopped skin
  • Fold with the rice paddle in slicing strokes until everything is evenly through — don't mash the grains.
  • Let it cool a few minutes, until you can hold it. Then tip in the cold ikura and fold gently once or twice — keep the eggs whole; don't mash them into paste.

steps.title: Mix into the rice, then the ikura

steps.body_html:
• Wet your palms, dip 2–3 fingertips in the salt and rub it over both palms.
  • Take about 100 g (½ cup) of the warm salmon–ikura rice in your left palm.
  • Press the triangle: right hand bent into a “mountain” on top, left hand cupping, turning a third each time — light, so it stays airy (see the onigiri page).
  • Wrap a nori strip round the bottom if you like. Re-wet and re-salt your hands for each one. Eat warm or at room temperature, within a few hours.
